sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Atlas is Northwind's new checkout and billing platform: catalog, cart, card payments, refunds, invoices and a customer account dashboard.

sections.heading: Team roster
sections.text: Priya Nair: product lead. Marcus Chen: backend and payments lead. Sofia Lindqvist: frontend and design. Wei Zhang: backend (tax, billing). Elena Rossi: QA. Tomas Alvarez: backend (inventory, refunds, data migration). Daniel Okafor: infrastructure and security. Aisha Khan: marketing and operations (launch communications, support). Owen Pierce: Finance and vendor management. Nadia Haddad: Legal counsel. Rafael Duarte: VP Product, chair of the steering committee.

sections.heading: External vendors
sections.text: PayGate provides the payments API. Halberd Security provides the external penetration test.

sections.heading: Where things live
sections.text: Tickets are tracked in Jira (ATL project). Specs, plans and decision logs live in Notion. Vendor and cross-team discussion happens by email.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: Version 1 of the Atlas launch specification, approved by product and engineering on 2026-05-20.

sections.heading: Launch date
sections.text: Target public GA date: 2026-09-15. The launch announcement follows GA in the same week.

sections.heading: Scope at GA
sections.text: Catalog and cart, card payments, refunds, invoice generation, customer account dashboard, and recurring (subscription) billing.

sections.heading: Dependencies
sections.text: Payments API v2 from PayGate and the external security review must both land before GA.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: Version 2 of the launch specification, revised by marketing. It replaces version 1 once it is approved. Approval is pending.

sections.heading: Launch date
sections.text: Public launch: 2026-10-06, aligned with the press agency embargo. The press release, customer emails and in-app announcements are scheduled around this date.

sections.heading: Scope at launch
sections.text: Catalog and cart, card payments, refunds, invoice generation and the customer account dashboard. Recurring billing is not part of launch scope.

sections.heading: Open items
sections.text: Final sign-off from product and the steering committee.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: Integrate PayGate payments API v2: authorize, capture, refund and webhooks. Tracked in ATL-112.

sections.heading: Original schedule
sections.text: Sandbox delivery from PayGate by 2026-06-10, then integration work by the checkout, refund, billing and test teams.

sections.heading: Downstream work
sections.text: Four workstreams depend on the sandbox: the card payment screen (ATL-118), refund workflow (ATL-121), end-to-end payment tests (ATL-127) and billing invoice generation (ATL-133).

sections.heading: Revision log
sections.text: 2026-06-18: sandbox delivery moved from 2026-06-10 to mid-July. The vendor has not yet provisioned the sandbox. Status is tracked in ATL-112.

title: Decision Log: Subscription billing descoped from Atlas GA

sections.heading: Decision
sections.text: Recurring (subscription) billing is removed from the Atlas GA scope and moved to Atlas 1.1, planned for Q4 2026.

sections.heading: Reason
sections.text: The payments API v2 launch scope covers one-off charges, refunds and webhooks only. The basic fraud rules (ATL-130) are not designed for recurring charges. Keeping subscriptions in scope would put the launch date at risk.

sections.heading: Decided by
sections.text: The steering committee, on 2026-05-28.

sections.heading: Impact
sections.text: The scope list in the launch specification no longer includes recurring billing. Existing one-off invoicing work continues.

title: Decision Log: Hosted card fields for checkout

sections.heading: Decision
sections.text: Card entry uses PayGate hosted card fields, so card numbers never touch Northwind servers.

sections.heading: Reason
sections.text: It keeps Atlas out of the heaviest PCI compliance scope and shortens the security review.

sections.heading: Decided by
sections.text: Marcus Chen and Daniel Okafor (security), on 2026-04-30.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.text: The card payment screen (ATL-118) is built around the hosted fields. Real card submission cannot be tested until the PayGate sandbox exists.

sections.heading: Status
sections.text: Complete. Refund workflow implementation signed off on 2026-06-19 and ready for release.

sections.heading: What it covers
sections.text: Customer refund requests, approvals and payouts.

sections.heading: Overall
sections.text: Amber. One critical dependency is outside the team's control.

sections.heading: Payments
sections.text: Payments API v2 is blocked on the vendor sandbox. New ETA is mid-July. Payment-dependent work is on hold.

sections.heading: Coming up
sections.text: Threat model review on 2026-06-30 (ATL-116). Staging environment upgrade due 2026-07-15 (ATL-138).

sections.heading: Risks
sections.text: Any further slip in the sandbox delivery moves the checkout, refund and billing work.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.text: Staging has been upgraded to production capacity and is ready for load testing.

sections.heading: Scenarios
sections.text: Peak checkout traffic, sustained browse load, and a coupon-heavy cart mix.

sections.heading: Schedule
sections.text: Run window 2026-06-08 to 2026-07-08, reported in ATL-124.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.text: Bottlenecks and latency percentiles go into the test report.

title: Security Review and Pen Test Plan

sections.heading: Threat model
sections.text: A checkout threat model is reviewed with the security team (ATL-116, review meeting on 2026-06-30).

sections.heading: Penetration test
sections.text: An external vendor, Halberd Security, tests the checkout and billing endpoints before launch. Scheduling is tracked in ATL-136.

sections.heading: Timing
sections.text: The test window depends on the vendor's availability.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.text: Onboard the first 20 beta customers and collect checkout feedback before launch.

sections.heading: Kickoff
sections.text: Beta kickoff is 2026-08-03.

sections.heading: Onboarding
sections.text: The customer list is selected and onboarding scheduled under ATL-140, due 2026-07-31.

sections.heading: Support
sections.text: Beta customers use the standard support escalation process.

sections.heading: Repository
sections.text: Atlas lives in a monorepo. Request access from infrastructure and clone it on day one.

sections.heading: Continuous integration
sections.text: Every pull request runs build and tests. Main is protected; CI must be green to merge.

sections.heading: Code review
sections.text: Every change needs one reviewer from another sub-team.

sections.heading: Local setup
sections.text: Use the provided container image so local and CI environments match.

sections.heading: Severity levels
sections.text: Sev 1: checkout down. Sev 2: degraded performance. Sev 3: minor defect.

sections.heading: On-call
sections.text: Infrastructure runs a weekly on-call rotation. The primary acknowledges pages within 10 minutes.

sections.heading: Communication
sections.text: Post updates in the incident channel every 30 minutes until resolved.

sections.heading: After the incident
sections.text: Write a short review within five working days.

sections.heading: Tokens
sections.text: Use the published color, spacing and typography tokens (ATL-104). Do not hard-code values.

sections.heading: Components
sections.text: Prefer existing components. Request new ones through the design channel.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.text: All components target WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard support.

sections.heading: US holidays
sections.text: Independence Day observed on 2026-07-03, Labor Day on 2026-09-07, Thanksgiving on 2026-11-26 and 2026-11-27.

sections.heading: Year end
sections.text: The office is closed from 2026-12-24 to 2026-12-31.

sections.heading: Requesting leave
sections.text: Submit leave requests at least two weeks ahead.

sections.heading: Tiers
sections.text: Tier 1 handles general questions. Tier 2 handles account and billing issues. Tier 3 is engineering.

sections.heading: Response targets
sections.text: Critical issues get a first reply within one hour, others within one working day.

sections.heading: Handoff
sections.text: Escalate with the customer's ticket reference and a short summary of steps already tried.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: Migrate legacy billing data in phases by customer cohort, with a full dry run in the test environment before each phase.

sections.heading: Invoice history
sections.text: Invoice history is mapped last, after customer records are verified. Mapping is in progress (ATL-134).

sections.heading: Cutover
sections.text: Final cutover happens after the beta program, with a rollback plan for each cohort.

sections.heading: Owner
sections.text: Tomas Alvarez owns the migration. Target completion is 2026-08-14.

sections.heading: Events
sections.text: Track page views, add-to-cart, checkout start, payment submitted and order confirmed.

sections.heading: Governance
sections.text: The data team approves any new event before it ships.

sections.heading: Fee and pricing changes
sections.text: Any change to a vendor fee schedule needs approval from Finance. Owen Pierce signs for Finance.

sections.heading: Liability and legal terms
sections.text: Legal reviews liability and indemnity terms before signature.

sections.heading: Signature
sections.text: Finance countersigns vendor contracts after Finance and Legal approve.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text: If a vendor misses a date, vendor management escalates to the vendor's account lead.
